observations: Three photos show stacks of bare automotive engines on wooden pallets inside what looks like a dim warehouse or workshop.
Engines appear to be V6 units with aluminum valve covers, timing covers, and accessory pulleys; some have an orange-colored residue/corrosion near the front cover and oil pan area.
Loose wiring harness ends hang disconnected from at least one engine in photo 0 and photo 1, with no sensors or connectors attached.
No serial number, engine code plate, or VIN sticker is legible in any photo.
Multiple engines are visible in the background of each shot, so it is unclear which single unit is the one being offered for sale.
A watermark 'POSTED ON JIJI - G.O MERCHANTS LTD' overlays all three photos.
No oil, no visible leaks beyond the orange residue, no compression test, no cold-start video, and no mileage sticker are shown.

identity.kind: used V6 car engine (bare, pulled, no transmission shown)

claims.evidence: No engine code plate, casting number, or VIN tag is visible in any photo to confirm this fitment.
Same as above; no identifying marks visible.
IS250 uses a different (smaller) engine than the V6 shown appears to be in these photos; no plate visible to confirm.
No casting/engine code visible to match Camry's four variants across those years.

risks.risk: Engine may not run or may have internal damage (seized, cracked block, bad bearings) since it is shown static with no start-up proof.
risks.proof: A video of the engine running/idling with oil pressure and no unusual noise or smoke.

risks.risk: Orange residue near the timing cover/oil pan could indicate rust from water exposure, coolant leak, or long outdoor storage, which can mean internal corrosion.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the residue area and the dipstick/oil color, plus the oil fill cap interior.

risks.risk: Loose, cut wiring suggests harness, sensors, or ECU components may be missing, which the buyer would need to source separately.
risks.proof: Photo of the full wiring harness and confirmation of which sensors/connectors are included.

risks.risk: It is unclear which engine among the several stacked units is actually being sold, risking a mismatch between what's pictured and what's delivered.
risks.proof: A photo with the specific unit tagged/marked and isolated from the others, plus a close-up of its casting number.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unverified unit, worst case assumed

risks.risk: No mileage or engine history (accident, flood, teardown reason) is disclosed.
risks.proof: Seller statement with a mileage sticker photo or prior vehicle documentation.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the engine code/casting number stamped on the block, matched to the unit actually for sale.
A start-up or running video of this specific engine.
Close-up of the orange residue area and the oil on the dipstick.
Photo showing the complete wiring harness and confirming no missing sensors/components.
Confirmation (photo) of which single engine in the stack is included in the sale.
response.reason: The photos show a used bare V6 engine with no readable engine code, no run-proof, visible corrosion, and cut wiring, so it must be priced at worst case as a non-verified, possibly non-running, incomplete unit until the seller provides engine-code and running proof.
